issues.legal_issue: A statutory compensation scheme for compulsory acquisition must use principles relevant to the value of the property at or about the time of acquisition.
material_facts: The acquisition law required compensation for the undertaking as a whole, calculated by valuing its assets under separate rules and deducting its liabilities.
Unused machinery in good condition was valued at its original purchase cost, even where that cost could be substantially below its value at acquisition.
Other machinery was valued at its written-down value under income-tax rules, which reflected notional depreciation allowances rather than the machinery's actual value.
Machinery was the most valuable part of the undertaking.
issues.conclusion: The machinery valuation rules were irrelevant to determining its value at acquisition and therefore did not provide compensation within the constitutional requirement; the acquisition law was unconstitutional.
issues.legal_principle: Under Article 31(2) of the Constitution, a law authorising compulsory acquisition had to provide a just equivalent or specify principles that would lead to that result. The principles themselves were subject to judicial scrutiny for relevance and arbitrariness, although the adequacy of compensation produced by relevant, non-arbitrary principles was not reviewable. A scheme was invalid if its compensation was illusory or its principles were unrelated to the property's value at or about acquisition. The Court relied on The State of West Bengal v. Mrs. Bela Banerjee, State of Madras v. D. Namasivaya Mudaliar, Vajravelu v. Special Deputy Collector, and Jeejeebhoy v. Assistant Collector.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_acquisition_: A party challenged the constitutional validity of a law authorising compulsory acquisition.
predicates.unused_machinery_valued_at_historical_co: The law valued unused machinery in good condition by its original purchase cost rather than its value at acquisition.
predicates.used_machinery_valued_by_tax_written_dow: The law valued used machinery by a written-down amount calculated for taxation purposes.
predicates.valuation_rules_unrelated_to_value_at_ac: The valuation methods did not reflect the property's value at or about the time it was acquired.

issues.definition: When an acquisition law is challenged and its machinery valuation methods are unrelated to value at acquisition, the law fails the compensation requirement.

issues.legal_issue: An invalid valuation principle for a major component of an undertaking cannot be severed from a single compensation scheme for the undertaking as a whole when the scheme does not provide separate compensation for its components.
material_facts: The law treated the compensation for the undertaking as a single compensation, although it prescribed different valuation principles for its assets.
Machinery was the most valuable part of the undertaking.
The defective machinery valuation principles affected the total compensation, and the Court found no basis to conclude that higher valuations for other assets would offset the deficiency.
issues.conclusion: The defective machinery valuation rule was not severable from the compensation scheme; the constitutional defect affected the compensation for the undertaking as a whole and rendered the law unconstitutional.
issues.legal_principle: Where an undertaking is acquired as a unit and compensation is prescribed as a single amount, the compensation principles for its constituent parts are not severable if an invalid principle governing a major part affects the total compensation. The Court applied that reasoning under Article 31(2) of the Constitution, in light of the compensation scheme and its conclusion that the machinery rules did not provide relevant valuation principles.

predicates.constitutional_challenge_to_acquisition_: A party challenged the constitutional validity of a law authorising compulsory acquisition.
predicates.compensation_is_single_for_entire_undert: The law provides one compensation amount for an undertaking acquired as a whole, though it values components separately.
predicates.invalid_valuation_rule_applies_to_major_: An invalid valuation rule applies to a component that makes up a major part of the undertaking.
predicates.valuation_rules_are_not_severable: The defective component valuation cannot be separated from the total compensation scheme.

issues.definition: When a challenged acquisition law provides single compensation for an undertaking and an inseverable invalid valuation rule affects a major component, the entire law is unconstitutional.
